title: Customer Risk Categorisation and Periodic Updation of KYC

paragraphs.text: Reference is invited to circular GZ-KYC-2019-01 dated April 15, 2019 on Customer Due Diligence. Banks are now advised to adopt a risk-based approach under which every customer is placed in a risk category and the KYC records of the customer are periodically updated at intervals linked to that risk category.

Customer risk categorisation shall place every customer in one of three categories, namely low risk, medium risk or high risk, based on the customer's identity, social and financial status, nature of business activity, location of the customer and its clients, mode of payment and expected turnover.

Customers who shall be classified as high risk include non-resident customers, Politically Exposed Persons, trusts and charities, firms with sleeping partners, dealers in high-value goods such as bullion and jewellery, and customers onboarded through non-face-to-face channels without subsequent verification.

Periodic updation of KYC (re-KYC) for high-risk customers shall be carried out at least once in every 24 months from the date of account opening or the date of the last KYC updation, whichever is later.

Periodic updation of KYC (re-KYC) for medium-risk customers shall be carried out at least once in every 84 months, and for low-risk customers at least once in every 120 months, from the date of account opening or the date of the last KYC updation, whichever is later.

The customer risk categorisation of every account shall be reviewed at least once in every six months and the reasons for any change in risk category shall be documented. The risk categorisation and periodic updation provisions of circular GZ-KYC-2019-02 shall be effective from October 1, 2019.
